sites.title: ASCEND Class Calendar
sites.audience: Office of Curricular Affairs staff, through their access code on the Hub.
sites.intro: For planning and review by the Office of Curricular Affairs only; not the schedule of record. The class schedule exactly as it stands in the Office of Curricular Affairs' Google Calendar, refreshed automatically every 30 minutes. Two small calendars for the current and next month sit at the top of every view; open on today's sessions with what is next up, see the week as a Monday-to-Friday board, or list every scheduled session grouped by module, by session type (LEC, SGD, CCSG, LAB, PNL, REV, INT and the assessments) or by week.

views.title: Today
views.blurb: The day at a glance: what is happening now or next, every session as a full card with time and type, and a preview of the next three class days. Opens by default.

views.title: Week
views.blurb: Monday to Friday, each session as a card, plus a strip of all-day items and quiz or pre-check windows that span several days.

views.title: All sessions
views.blurb: Every scheduled session from today onward (or the whole calendar), grouped by module, by session type or by week, with each group collapsible. Combine with the module or type filter to see one module's or one type's full schedule.

views.title: Cohort, module and type filters
views.blurb: Switch between class calendars (Class of 2029 and Class of 2030 in Phase 1, Class of 2027 in Year 4), pick one module, choose session types or assessments from a dropdown, show only mandatory sessions, or search any session by name.

views.title: Contact hours
views.blurb: A button on the calendar that totals the scheduled hours for a module, or for every module, in an academic year: instructional and assessment hours, a table by session type, and a CSV download. A planning estimate from the published calendar.

sites.title: Clinical Skills Portal
sites.audience: Clinical Skills: curriculum leadership, the governance committees that oversee clinical skills, and Clinical Competency Mentors. Clinical Skills Rubrics: a smaller group of faculty and staff, because it holds standardized-patient checklists, faculty-only rubrics and quiz answer keys. Clinical Skills Milestones: everyone who can open the portal (curriculum content, no student data). All three sit behind the portal's own server-side gate; your Hub code opens what your role allows.
sites.intro: Three separate dashboards behind one access code. Two cover the Practice of Medicine and PEAKS 1, linked by skill domain: how each class performed in each clinical skill, and the checklists, rubrics and quizzes that produced those scores. Each class runs POM 1 (August) to PEAKS 1 (December of the following year). The third, Clinical Skills Milestones, follows nine clinical skill strands across all three phases, from POM to residency.

views.title: Clinical Skills: Dashboard
views.blurb: Each class's strongest and weakest skill domains across POM 1, 2, 3 and PEAKS 1, with class comparison.

views.title: Clinical Skills: Analytics
views.blurb: Performance by skill, framework, quartile band or faculty group, with sortable heatmaps.

views.title: Clinical Skills: Frameworks
views.blurb: The six skill domains mapped to MEPOs, AAMC competencies, Core EPAs and communication functions.

views.title: Rubrics: Library and items
views.blurb: Every POM checklist, rubric, scoring guide and quiz answer key by class and term, searchable to the single item (faculty and staff only).

views.title: Rubrics: Crosswalk and Compare
views.blurb: One skill across every rubric that scores it, and any two deliveries of a rubric side by side.

views.title: Clinical Skills Milestones
views.blurb: Nine clinical skill strands across the three phase gates: the milestone at each gate, the behaviors a rater checks, where it is taught, in-course assessment and the PEAKS gate assessment (PEAKS III is the TTR final assessment).

It follows that competency from the end of Phase 1 to residency readiness, and marks what is already taught and what is proposed.

sites.title: Meeting Minutes Generator
sites.audience: Office of Curricular Affairs staff and governance support. Not for EEC, subcommittee or Monday Curricular Affairs minutes: those stay in the Governance dashboard.
sites.intro: Drop in the transcript Zoom or Teams makes of a meeting, or paste its text, and get a Word draft of the minutes straight away for you to edit. Nothing else to fill in; nothing you upload is stored. Your Hub code opens it.

views.title: Add the transcript
views.blurb: Drop a Zoom “Audio transcript” (.vtt) or a Teams transcript (.docx or .vtt), or paste the transcript text into the box.

views.title: Claude drafts the minutes
views.blurb: Overview, decisions, action items with owners and due dates, discussion by topic, and open questions. Student names are left out.

views.title: Edit the Word draft
views.blurb: The draft downloads as Word, marked DRAFT. Check names, who said what and the action-item owners, then send it.

sites.title: Remove Student Names
sites.audience: Office of Curricular Affairs staff, dashboard maintainers and governance support, before a file with student names is shared or dropped in a dashboard inbox. Not for Student Performance: its owner keeps that data.
sites.intro: Most dashboard files start with student names, like Blackboard gradebooks. This site takes the names, usernames, IDs and emails out before the file goes in an inbox, so Claude only ever sees codes. It reads the file inside your browser: nothing is uploaded or stored. Your Hub code opens it.

views.title: Choose the file
views.blurb: A Blackboard gradebook, NBME score download, one45 or CPEvals export, or a Registrar workbook (.xlsx, .xls, .csv, .txt). A practice file with made-up students is built in.

views.title: Check what it found
views.blurb: Columns that show who a student is are ticked, by heading or by what they hold. Look across every column, then tick or untick.

views.title: No key or with a key
views.blurb: No key for Phase 1 and Electives (S001, S002…). With a key for Phase 2, NBME, Clinical Skills and MEPO, so the same student gets the same code in every file.

views.title: Save the DEID file
views.blurb: The cleaned file saves to your Downloads, named … DEID. Put it in the dashboard's inbox and delete the original.

sites.title: ASCEND Program Evaluation Report Generator
sites.audience: Office of Curricular Affairs staff and the subcommittee that reviews module evaluations. The exports rate named educators, so only some Hub codes open it.
sites.intro: Upload a module's one45 evaluation export and get the Module Evaluation Report as a Word file: a one-page summary, rating charts, last year's ratings for comparison, themes from student comments, educator ratings and the verbatim module comments. Nothing you upload is stored. Your Hub code opens it.

views.title: Upload the one45 export
views.blurb: The module's evaluation export (.xlsx). The site recognizes the module and fills in the cohort, dates and response counts.

views.title: Review the comment themes
views.blurb: Claude groups every student comment into themes; each needs three or more students. Read the quotes behind a theme, rename it or remove it.

views.title: Download the Word report
views.blurb: In the Office of Curricular Affairs layout, with 2024-25 and 2025-26 ratings for comparison where the one45 summaries have them.
